a-stĭtŭo (better than adst- ), ŭi, ūtum, 3, v. a. statuo,
I.to place a person or thing somewhere (very rare, perh. only in the foll. exs.): “Juben an non jubes astitui aulas?” Plaut. Capt. 4, 2, 66 Fleck.: reum ad lectum ejus (aegroti) astituemus, Auct. ad Her. 3, 20 B. and K.; App. M. 9, p. 222, 1; 3, p. 130.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
